items.stem: Complete the statement: Allocation of overheads means …
options: charging overheads to units of output
charging an overhead in full to the one cost centre that caused it
sharing an overhead between cost centres on a fair basis
items.answer: charging an overhead in full to the one cost centre that caused it
items.markingKey: charging an overhead in full to the one cost centre that caused it. Wholly incurred by one centre [1]

items.stem: Distinguish between allocation and apportionment of overheads.
items.answer: Allocation charges a whole overhead to one cost centre that incurred it; apportionment shares an overhead that benefits several centres using a fair basis.
items.markingKey: Allocation – one centre [1]; apportionment – shared on a basis [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why the basis chosen for apportionment should reflect the benefit each cost centre receives.
items.answer: So that each department bears a fair share of overheads, giving more accurate product costs and prices.
items.markingKey: Fair share/causal link [1]; accurate product cost [1] [2]

items.answer: budgeted overheads ÷ budgeted activity

items.stem: Explain why a labour-hour rate may be preferred in a labour-intensive department.
items.answer: Most overheads (supervision, canteen) relate to labour time, so jobs using more labour hours should absorb more overheads.
items.markingKey: Overheads linked to labour [1]; fair absorption [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain why a business uses predetermined (budgeted) absorption rates.
items.answer: Actual overheads and activity are not known until the year end; a predetermined rate allows product costs and prices to be calculated as jobs are done.
items.markingKey: Actual not known [1]; costs/prices during year [1] [2]

items.stem: Explain two causes of under-absorption of overheads.
items.answer: Actual overheads were higher than budgeted; actual activity (hours) was lower than budgeted; or both.

items.stem: Explain how an over-absorption is treated in the financial statements.
items.answer: Too much overhead was charged to production, so the excess is credited to the income statement (reducing cost of sales), increasing profit.
items.markingKey: Excess charged [1]; credited to IS/profit up [1] [2]

items.stem: Baobab Furnishings has two production departments, Pressing and Painting. Overheads allocated directly: Pressing $12,100, Painting $9,100. items.stem: Baobab Furnishings has two production departments. Machining is machine intensive: budgeted overheads $185,000, budgeted machine hours 15,500. Assembly is labour intensive: budgeted overheads $47,000, budgeted direct labour hours 14,500. The owner calculated the Machining absorption rate as $7.73 per hour. Identify the error and state the correct absorption rate.
items.answer: A single blanket rate was used for both departments; each department needs its own rate based on its main activity. Correct absorption rate: $11.94 per machine hour.

items.stem: Lagoon Boatworks has two production departments. Cutting is machine intensive: budgeted overheads $117,000, budgeted machine hours 16,500. Finishing is labour intensive: budgeted overheads $142,000, budgeted direct labour hours 11,000. (a) Calculate a suitable overhead absorption rate for each department. (b) Evaluate whether Lagoon Boatworks should use a single factory-wide absorption rate instead of departmental rates.
items.answer: (a) Cutting $7.09 per machine hour; Finishing $12.91 per labour hour (b) A single rate is simpler but may misallocate overheads when departments differ (machine v labour intensive); departmental rates are more accurate.

items.stem: Kilimanjaro Coffee budgeted overheads of $129,000 and 5,500 machine hours for the year. Actual overheads were $131,000 and actual machine hours were 7,000. A student calculated the under/over-absorption as $2,000. State the mistake made and give the correct under/over-absorption.
items.answer: Budgeted overheads were compared with actual overheads; absorbed overheads (actual hours × OAR) must be compared with actual overheads. Correct under/over-absorption: over-absorbed $33,182.
items.markingKey: Error: budgeted overheads were compared with actual overheads; absorbed overheads (actual hours × OAR) must be compared with actual overheads [1]; correct under/over-absorption: over-absorbed $33,182 [1] [2]
